findings.issue: P125-R23's issue named two things: the remote steps recorded done, and 'the local tag step has already run too'. The fix resolves the first (remote steps are now recorded `skipped` and run on a later --push run; rl2b/rl2c/rl2e cover this). The second still happens. `tag` is not in REMOTE_STEPS, so a run without --push still creates the annotated `v<version>` tag locally after wait-ci was skipped, before any CI run has seen that commit. The second, --push run finds `tag` done and pushes that tag after CI goes green. If CI goes red on the publish run, the local tag already sits on the rejected commit. The resume cannot move it, and preflight on a fresh state file refuses because the tag exists. The finding's chosen resolution option is still met, so this is a carried residue, not a contradicted clause.
findings.resolution: Carry. Either treat `tag` like the remote steps when --push is absent (record it `skipped`, so the tag is cut only after wait-ci is green on the publish run), or state in the module docstring that a prepare run tags locally before CI. Add a rl2-family assertion that a no-push run issues no `git tag -a`, or expects one.

findings.issue: wait-ci now waits on the `ciSha` recorded at push time, and `push-ci-branch` is `done` once it has run. When CI is red because of a real defect, the fix is an amended release commit. A resume never re-pushes it: push-ci-branch is done. It also cannot follow a hand re-push of ci/v<version>: the recorded ciSha wins over origin/<branch>, so wait-ci keeps reading the old failed run. Recovery only works for a re-run of the same commit, which is what rl4 models. Recovery was already broken before this diff, because the bare rev-parse never resolved. This diff pins it to the stale SHA.
findings.resolution: Carry. When wait-ci ends red (failure, not cancelled), clear `ciSha` and set push-ci-branch back to pending, so the resume pushes HEAD again and re-dispatches. Or, on resume, resolve origin/<branch> in preference to a recorded SHA that HEAD has moved past. Add a rl case: red CI, amend (fake HEAD changes), resume, and expect a second push and a wait on the new SHA.
